# screenshotpro
**Annotated UI screenshots whose coordinates are measured, not drawn by hand.**
**English** | 中文
Every rectangle in that figure was measured, not drawn — and it only shipped because all 15 assertio
angle in that figure was measured, not drawn — and it only shipped because all 15 assertions passed.

You give it a Windows executable. It launches the app, captures the whole window with
`PrintWindow`,

dumps the entire UI Automation control tree, and stores both. A JSON spec
then says *which* control

to point at — never *where* it is. The renderer turns that into
a figure with boxes, numbered badge

s, arrows, pixelated secrets and a legend bar; the
verifier proves the figure with 15 assertions and
exits non-zero if any of them breaks.
It ships as two things that do not depend on each other:
| Form | What you get | Needs DSH? |
| **Standalone CLI** | `python tools/render.py` + `tools/verify.py` (+ `tools/measure_win.py` on Win

dows) | No — Python 3.9+ and Pillow |
| **DSH plugin bundle** | A `Screenshot Pro` agent preset that
mounts this skill and the tools it needs | Yes — any DSH host |
## Demo figures

The two figures below were rendered from **public web pages**, and every rectangle came out of
the l

ive DOM (`getBoundingClientRect`) — not one coordinate in either `spec.json` was typed by
hand. Both
are reproducible offline from the files committed in `demo/`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### Wikipedia — a reading path through an article

Four steps: the top-bar search box, the language switcher, the left-hand table of contents, and
an i

nline link in the body text. The account area is pixelated. Notice where the text lives: the
copy si
ts in the **legend bar underneath**, so the article itself is never written over.
### MDN — search and navigation

Three steps: the search pill, the JavaScript nav tab, and an inline link in the hero. The
third-part

y ad strip is pixelated. This figure was rendered with the opt-in
`style.badge_avoid_dense_pixels` s

witch on — see `demo/README.md` for why it helped here and
did **not** help on the Wikipedia figure.
## The rule the whole repo is built around
> **Coordinates are measured, never estimated.**

Every rectangle comes from UI Automation data in `dump.json`. Nothing is hand-tuned,
rescaled or nud

ged. If a rectangle is wrong, the bug is in the measurement step — not in
the spec, and never in the

renderer. This is why the pipeline can be verified at all:
assertion 3 compares the report against

the dump field by field, and assertion 8 fails
when a box lands on blank pixels, which is exactly wh
at a guessed coordinate produces.
## Capability table
| Stage | Standalone command | Reads | Writes | Contract |
| Measure | `python tools/measure_win.py --exe <app.exe> --out figures/<name>` | the running app (UI
Automation) | `shot.png`, `dump.json`, `measure-log.txt` | `dump.schema = uia-dump/1`, `shot` size

== window rect, `image_rect == screen_rect - window origin` |
| Annotate | `python tools/render.py f
igures/<name>/spec.json` | `spec.json`, `shot.png`, `dump.json` | `out/<name>.png`, `out/render-repo

rt.json` | `spec.schema = annot-spec/1`, output width == input width |
| Verify | `python tools/veri
fy.py figures/<name>/spec.json` | the spec, the dump, the report, the rendered PNG | a PASS/FAIL tab

le | exit `0` only when all 15 assertions pass |
| Self-test | `python tests/run_tests.py` | nothing
— it builds its own synthetic fixture | fixture + figure in a temp dir | 15/15 PASS, plus a deliber
ately broken report that must FAIL |

Figure features: highlighted boxes with padding, numbered circular badges that avoid
collisions and

refuse to cover a control, arrows from badge to box edge, `pixelate`
redaction of a measured control

rect, and an auto-sized legend bar appended under the
screenshot (canvas width never changes).
## Install
### As a DSH plugin
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then, in the same profile directory (`~/.dsh/profiles/<name>/`):

1. add `screenshotpro` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in `package.json`
2. set the one `customSkillDirs` l
ine below to the **absolute path** of this package's `skills/`

Restart DSH: the `Screenshot Pro` preset and the `screenshot-pro` skill show up in the catalog.
Noth
ing is compiled, nothing is bundled — the package is Python source plus one YAML patch.

`package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, and `cordis.patch.yml` inserts one agent preset
(`Screen

shot Pro`) that mounts `@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill`,
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-

skill-filesystem`, a shell for the current platform, file/job/todo/ask-user
tools, and adds this rep
o's `skills/` directory as a skill root.

**You must edit one line before installing.** `dsh-skill-filesystem` resolves every entry of
`config

.customSkillDirs` with `node:path.resolve()`, so a relative path would resolve against
the DSH host'

s process cwd instead of this package, and no placeholder is expanded
(source: `dsh-skill-filesystem

/lib/index.js` — `customSkillDirs: z.array(z.string())` and
`(config.customSkillDirs ?? []).map((roo

t) => resolve(root))`). Put the absolute path of
this repo's `skills/` directory there:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

After that the preset is complete; add it to a profile like any other bundle and the
`screenshot-pro
` skill appears in the session catalog.
